title: Rust
subtitle: Rust is my systems language: about a million and a half lines across the governance platform, the agent runtime, the collaboration shell, the memory gateway, the execution substrate and the inference pipeline.

stats.label: lines of Rust in AgentOS, across nineteen crates
unsafe blocks in the capabilities model, all in one FFI module
domain modules split from two 40,000-line hook files
steps every Agent Swarm tool call passes, in a frozen order

lede: AgentOS had to make AI agents follow rules they could not talk their way around, so I put the rules in compiled code. The database layer and the hook binary are around 200,000 lines each. The hook binary runs under the coding agents' own command-line tools and turns policy into refusals. A refusal is a typed value that can only name a command the system sanctions, so the compiler stops an agent from ever being told to run a command that does not exist. When two hook source files grew too large, I had them split into domain modules under a symbol-parity check. See Why long agent runs fail.
quote: I put invariants in types wherever the compiler can enforce them.
evidence: Rust systems engineering: about 546,000 lines of Rust in a governance control plane, where a refusal is a typed value that can only name a command the system sanctions.
Unsafe code containment and FFI: 121 unsafe blocks confined to one FFI module over CUDA, with layout tests that fail the build if the Rust and C views disagree.
Concurrency design in Rust: a synchronous single-owner hot loop for a 24,000-line token-aware broker, and async Tokio for the voice engine and the transports that wait on I/O.
Build-enforced invariants: link-time registration that fails the build for an unwired function, and 12 frozen pipeline steps on every Agent Swarm tool call.
author: Corey James
